blocks.content: This topic formalizes spec.template, seen throughout the Deployments, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, and Jobs modules, an embedded Pod spec used as a repeatable stamp, not a live object in its own right.
As first previewed in the Deployments module, spec.template is, structurally, an entire Pod spec, the exact same shape covered throughout the Pods module, embedded inside a larger, managing object.

blocks.alt: The exact same Pod spec structure from the Pods module, embedded inside something larger

blocks.content: The name is deliberate and precise, a template is not itself a live, running object, it is a stamp used to create many actual Pods from, exactly the way a cookie cutter shapes many cookies without being a cookie itself.

blocks.alt: A stamp used to create many real objects, never a live object on its own

blocks.content: This same pattern appears consistently across Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, and Job, covered across several modules, each uses spec.template the exact same structural way, to define what its managed Pods should actually look like.

blocks.alt: The exact same structural pattern, reused consistently across several workload types

blocks.content: This connects directly to the Rolling Update topic, changing a Deployment's template (a new image, a changed environment variable) is exactly what triggers the rolling update mechanism covered in full detail there.

blocks.alt: The exact trigger behind the rolling update mechanism covered in its own dedicated topic

blocks.content: Exactly the requirement covered in the Deployment Manifest topic, the template's own metadata.labels must match the parent object's selector, this is not optional, it is how the parent actually finds and manages the Pods it creates.

blocks.alt: A real, enforced requirement, not an optional convention, covered in the Deployments module

blocks.content:
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app   # must match the selector above

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: spec.template is an embedded Pod spec used as a repeatable stamp, not a live object itself, the same pattern reused across Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, and Job.
Changing the template triggers a rollout, and its labels must match the parent's selector exactly, a real, enforced requirement, not just a convention.
